h1: Wasp & Hornet Nest Removal Cost Guide
dek: How much does wasp or hornet nest removal cost? See prices by nest location and type, plus what actually affects your quote.
answer: Most homeowners pay $300–$700 to remove a wasp or hornet nest, with published industry averages around $525. Small, easy-to-reach exterior nests can run as low as $100–$200, while yellowjacket nests concealed underground or inside walls often reach $500–$1,200 because of the extra access work and labor involved.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to remove a wasp nest from a house?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most homeowners pay $100–$500, depending on where the nest is located. Easy-to-reach exterior nests are on the lower end, while nests in walls, attics, or high rooflines cost more due to added labor and equipment.

mainEntity.name: Is hornet nest removal more expensive than wasp nest removal?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be, since hornets are more aggressive and often require extra protective equipment and more careful timing. The bigger cost driver, though, is usually nest location rather than species alone.

mainEntity.name: Can I remove a wasp nest myself to save money?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a small, low, easily reached nest, some homeowners do it themselves with store-bought sprays, though this carries real sting risk. For nests in walls, attics, or high locations, or for larger colonies, professional removal is strongly recommended.

mainEntity.name: Why do nests inside walls cost more to remove?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treating a nest inside a wall void or attic often requires locating the exact spot, sometimes opening a small access point, and using specialized application methods to reach insects a surface spray can't. This added time and equipment increases the cost.

mainEntity.name: Will the wasps come back after removal?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the nest and queen are fully treated, wasps generally won't rebuild in that exact spot, though new wasps may build a nest elsewhere on the property in future seasons. Many companies offer a short-term guarantee if activity continues after treatment.

mainEntity.name: Is bee removal priced the same as wasp removal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not usually. Because honeybees are important pollinators, many companies use live-removal and relocation services for bees rather than extermination, which can be priced differently than standard wasp or hornet treatment. Published ranges put beehive removal at $135–$1,065, with most homeowners paying around $445, versus about $300–$700 for a typical wasp nest. Some local beekeepers will even relocate a honeybee swarm for free, so ask before you pay.
